Increasing num- bers of infants and children are receiving anticoagulants for prophylaxis and treatment of thromboembolism. Doses of war- farin and therapeutic INR ranges have been adapted from adult therapy but cohort studies1,2 of paediatric patients have found that warfarin requirements may be affected by a number of fac- tors including age, and the use of infant formulas supplemented with vitamin K. Recommendations3 for the use of oral anticoag- ulants in children have been published. 1. Tait RC, et al. Oral anticoagulation in paediatric patients: dose requirements and complications.
